extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent applicants, and EPO examiners (practitioners involved in drafting, prosecuting, or examining European patent claims)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to draft, interpret and examine claims under Article 84 EPC focusing on clarity, interpretation, and related formal/semantic issues that affect claim scope and validity. Covers many claim-drafting pitfalls and specific term/phrase treatments (e.g. 'comprising', product-by-process, negative limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.1 Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of the claims: whether the claims are clear in themselves and define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.1 (EPO website). Assess whether wording of claims is precise and unambiguous so a skilled person can understand the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2 Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for interpreting claims: how claim language should be understood when determining scope, including the role of the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.2. Consider literal wording first, then description/drawings for interpretation; avoid importing unrelated limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3 Inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and treatment of inconsistencies between claims and between claims and the description/drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.3. Determine whether inconsistencies create lack of clarity or contradict claim scope, and whether amendment or correction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.4 General statements, "spirit of the invention", claim-like clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and problems of general statements or 'spirit of the invention' language and clauses in claims that resemble general or non-limiting formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.4. Such general or aspirational language is not an adequate substitute for clear, limiting claim features.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.5 Essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of which features are essential to the invention and must be included in the claims for clarity and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.5. Identify essential features from the invention disclosure and ensure claims reflect them; omission may cause lack of clarity or insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.6 Relative terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of relative terms (e.g. 'upper', 'substantially', 'approximately') and requirement to make them clear by reference or definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.6. Relative terms must be used in a way that a skilled person can determine their meaning in the context.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.7 Terms such as "about", "approximately" or "substantially"
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation and permissibility of vague qualifiers such as 'about', 'approximately' or 'substantially' in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.7. Such terms may be acceptable if their meaning is clear from the description or common general knowledge; avoid undue vagueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.8 Trade marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of trade marks or brand names in claims and how they affect clarity and claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.8. Trade marks are not technical features per se and may need clarification or replacement by descriptive terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.9 Optional features
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of optional (non-essential) features in claims and the effect on scope and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.9. Clarify whether features are optional or mandatory; ambiguous optionality may cause interpretation problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.10 Result to be achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that define an invention by the result to be achieved rather than by structural or functional features, and the limits of such formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.10. A result-only definition may be unclear unless accompanied by means to achieve it or sufficiently defined functional features.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.11 Parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and definition of parameters (numerical ranges, measured values) in claims and how to ensure reproducible interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.11. Parameters should be defined clearly (units, measurement method) and supported by the description to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.12 Product-by-process claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment and interpretation of product-by-process claims which define a product in terms of the process by which it is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.12. Assess clarity and patentability implications; product-by-process may limit protection to products obtainable by the claimed process unless defined otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.13 Interpretation of expressions stating a purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: How expressions that state a purpose or intended use are interpreted in claims and their effect on scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.13. Purpose statements are generally not limiting unless the claim is drafted as a use claim or purpose is essential for technical character.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.14 Definition by reference to (use with) another entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Defining features by reference to another entity (e.g. 'use with X') and the clarity issues that may arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.14. Ensure referenced entities are identifiable and that the relationship defines the claimed subject-matter clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.15 The expression "in"
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation issues arising from the preposition 'in' (e.g. 'in a container', 'in a composition') within claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.15. The meaning of 'in' depends on context; clarify whether it denotes inclusion, containment, admixture, or other relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.16 Use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and interpretation of use claims (including second medical use claims), and requirements for clarity and permissible claim formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.16. Follow established EPO approaches for use claims (e.g. purpose-limited product claims) and ensure clarity of therapeutic use or technical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.17 References to the description or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissibility and effect of incorporating or referencing the description or drawings in claims for interpretation and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.17. Claims should be clear in themselves; excessive reliance on description/drawings for basic meaning may be problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.18 Reference signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and treatment of reference signs (numerals/letters pointing to drawings) in claims and their impact on claim scope and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.18. Reference signs are generally ignored in defining claim scope but may help clarity; they should not be construed as limiting features.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.19 Negative limitations (e.g. disclaimers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use, clarity and acceptability of negative claim limitations or disclaimers (expressing that the invention excludes certain features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.19. Negative limitations may be allowable but must be clear and supported; certain disclaimers have special legal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.20 "Comprising" vs. "consisting of"
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in claim scope and interpretation between open terms (e.g. 'comprising') and closed terms (e.g. 'consisting of').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.20. Use of 'comprising' typically indicates an open list (allows further elements), while 'consisting of' is limiting; choose term to reflect intended scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.21 Functional definition of a pathological condition
rubrics_metrics.description: How pathological conditions may be defined functionally in claims (e.g. by symptoms, markers) and the clarity/support issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.21. Functional definitions should be precise and supported by disclosure to ensure a skilled person can apply the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.22 Broad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems and considerations when claims are drafted broadly, including clarity, support, and potential overreach relative to the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.22. Broad claims must still be clear and supported; overly broad formulations risk objections under Article 84 or added subject-matter rules when amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.23 Order of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and substantive issues related to the ordering of claims and presentation (independent vs dependent claims, grouping, priority of claim sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.23. Ensure logical ordering and dependency structure to aid clarity and proper examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.24 Interpretation of terms such as identity and similarity in relation to amino or nucleic acid sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: How terms like 'identity' and 'similarity' should be interpreted for biological sequence claims and what must be defined for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See EPO Guidelines GL F IV 4.24. Provide clear definitions and measures (e.g. percentage identity, alignment method) so the scope is reproducible by a skilled person.
